newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt, opposition tied on FEC committee.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt, opposition tied on FEC committee.

text.p: The New Zealand government and the opposition will be evenly matched on the powerful finance and expenditure select committee (FEC) if parliament accepts the business committee's recommendation tabled in parliament on Wednesday.
But with free-market Act and centrist United holding two of the seats on the expanded 12-person committee, the government should see its nomination win the chair.

Act deputy leader Ken Shirley has said the coalition government has reached a political understanding with Act which will give Act one chair, possibly foreign affairs, in return for Act's support for the government's other nominations.
National would have four seats on the FEC, its New Zealand First coalition partner two, Act and United one each, Labour three and the Alliance one, if the recommendation was accepted.
National MP Tony Ryall is tipped to chair the FEC.

The business committee has also expanded to 10 from the normal eight the number of seats it recommends on the health, government administration, justice and law reform, and social services committees.
Maori affairs will have nine members, as will the standing orders committee.

The only committees where the government and the Labour and Alliance opposition parties are evenly matched are the regulations review, privileges, internal affairs and local government and officers of parliament committees.
